indicators.label: Deaths within 30 days
indicators.note: Deaths within 30 days of the crash. Up to 2010 DGT estimated them from deaths within 24 hours with correction factors; from 2011 it counts them by matching crash records with the register of deaths.

indicators.label: Deaths within 24 hours
indicators.note: Deaths within 24 hours of the crash, counted by the police in every year.

indicators.label: People admitted to hospital
indicators.note: Injured people admitted to hospital, counted within 30 days of the crash (DGT yearbook).

indicators.label: Injury crashes
indicators.note: Crashes with at least one person killed or injured, as recorded by the police. Crashes with no injury are not counted.

indicators.label: Injury crashes on interurban roads
indicators.note: Injury crashes on roads outside towns.

indicators.label: Injury crashes in urban areas
indicators.note: Injury crashes on urban streets and roads within towns.

indicators.label: Deaths per million residents
indicators.note: Deaths within 30 days of the crash. Up to 2010 DGT estimated them from deaths within 24 hours with correction factors; from 2011 it counts them by matching crash records with the register of deaths. Residents: INE population on 1 July.
indicators.unit: deaths within 30 days per million residents

indicators.label: Deaths per 100,000 registered vehicles
indicators.note: Deaths within 30 days of the crash. Up to 2010 DGT estimated them from deaths within 24 hours with correction factors; from 2011 it counts them by matching crash records with the register of deaths. Vehicles: DGT's registered fleet, which includes vehicles that are seldom driven.
indicators.unit: deaths within 30 days per 100,000 registered vehicles

indicators.label: Deaths per 100,000 tonnes of road fuel sold
indicators.note: Deaths within 30 days of the crash. Up to 2010 DGT estimated them from deaths within 24 hours with correction factors; from 2011 it counts them by matching crash records with the register of deaths. Road fuel (petrol and diesel sold for road use, CORES) stands in for traffic on all roads; it is not a measure of distance.
indicators.unit: deaths within 30 days per 100,000 tonnes of road fuel sold

indicators.label: Deaths per 100 injury crashes
indicators.note: Deaths within 30 days of the crash. Up to 2010 DGT estimated them from deaths within 24 hours with correction factors; from 2011 it counts them by matching crash records with the register of deaths. The ratio says how deadly recorded injury crashes were, not how often they happened.
indicators.unit: deaths within 30 days per 100 injury crashes

indicators.label: Interurban deaths per billion vehicle-km
indicators.note: Deaths within 30 days on interurban roads against the vehicle-kilometres the Ministerio de Transportes measures on the State, regional and provincial networks, which cover nearly the same roads. Only the years whose kilometres are comparable are shown; the latest year is partly estimated in the source.
indicators.unit: deaths on interurban roads per billion vehicle-kilometres measured on them
